speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; to begin our assessment, how long has this lesion been present, and have you noticed any recent changes in its size, color, or drainage?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes, and recent uveitis treatment, could you tell me if you have been taking any systemic or topical immunosuppressive medications? Additionally, is the ulcer on your right leg accompanied by warmth, redness, or significant swelling?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum.

The combination of a painful ulcer with a necrotic base and purplish borders, appearing at a site of minor trauma (ant bite) in a patient with Crohn's disease and diabetes, is highly characteristic of pyoderma gangrenosum. This clinical picture suggests an inflammatory response to the initial trauma rather than an infectious etiology.
